title: Layer-1 document-format item (one canonical-JSON line per format item)
description: Machine-readable contract for governance/doc-format/doc-format.jsonl - the Layer-1 (L1) document-format canon. THIS FILE + the JSONL it validates ARE the 'Layer-1 document-format definition' referenced by ADR 0014 §2 and ADR 0019. L1 is LANGUAGE-INDEPENDENT and ITEM-LEVEL: it fixes the MECE set of doc-set items (sections / structural members), each item's role, and its per-item applicability (the document analog of code's platform_scope / consumers, enabling mechanical impact). L1 is LIGHT - structural only, NO content hash. The three-layer model (baseline §10 M10): L1 format (here) -> L2 language template (governance/templates/<family>-*; common content vendored from the spec home governance/spec/<family>.md) -> L3 rendered doc-set. The heavy marker+hash machinery localizes to L2-common 'vendored' items only; L1/L3 stay light structural conformance. SCOPE (ADR 0014 §2, master-ownership discriminator): L1 governs documents (human/AI-facing prose - README/README.ja/SPEC/TESTING/CHANGELOG, community-health, the .github PR template) and repo-structural dotfiles that have NO master elsewhere (.gitattributes/.gitignore/workflows). It does NOT govern tool-owned configuration (e.g. .psa.config.json), whose master is the owning tool canon and which consumers follow-latest from it (ADR 0009), not a reconstructed template - the discriminator is: an artifact whose master another canon already owns is referenced/followed, never re-mastered here. A tool's own doc-set (e.g. psa.py README/SPEC) may be FORMAT-conformance-checked against L1 yet stays content-owned by the tool. CONSUMERS: the L2 templates conform to L1; the document-conformance gate (ADR 0014 §2, built at TF) reads L1 as ground truth for item-membership + applicability resolution. VERSIONING: governance/doc-format/VERSION is the L1 SemVer (the 'layer-1-format' front-matter pin, ADR 0019); 0.1.0 pre-release, promoted to 1.0.0 at the TF freeze (mirroring the code canon and the L2 governance/templates/VERSION).
$comment: AI read-contract: this is the authoritative, machine-checkable definition of WHICH items a governed doc-set is made of and WHERE each applies (by family / topology / presence). Edit only via the per-phase loop with [AUTH]; the conformance gate validates rendered doc-sets against the JSONL this schema constrains. NOT in scope: tool-owned configs (master-ownership rule above), and the authoring scaffolding (adr/prompt templates, GAP-4). Do NOT add content hashes to L1 items - heavy machinery is reserved for L2 'vendored' items (ADR 0015 markers in the spec home).

schema_version.description: L1 item record-shape era; lets the L1 tier evolve its columns independently under schema-on-read (mirrors the manifest convention). Initial value "1".

item_id.description: Primary key. Member-prefixed, dotted, lowercase-kebab identifier (the member prefix may itself contain a hyphen, e.g. community-health) (e.g. readme.ci-status-table, spec.part-a.reference-assets, changelog.format). Unique across the canon (MECE: no overlap).

member.description: The doc-set member this item belongs to. README.ja is NOT a separate member - it is the lock-step mirror of README, expressed by the per-item 'bilingual' flag.

order.description: Ordinal position of this item within its member (MECE ordering; unique within a member). Used for rendered-section sequencing.

role.description: Short human label for what this item is / does.

content_model.description: How the item's content is produced. common-fixed = identical verbatim across consumers (template renders it as-is, e.g. CHANGELOG format header, .gitattributes encoding contract). common-parameterized = common structure with {{TOKEN}} substitution (README spine, CI badge table, workflows). vendored = common content VENDORED from the L2-common spec home governance/spec/<family>.md via ADR 0015 markers + normalized hash (the ONLY items carrying heavy machinery; e.g. SPEC Part A). specific = per-consumer authored content (e.g. SPEC Part B, README action/phase refs, CHANGELOG entries). mixed = a common skeleton with consumer-specific fill.

bilingual.description: Whether this item participates in the README.md / README.ja.md lock-step pair (AGENTS.md §5 bilingual lock-step). Meaningful for member=readme; false for the English-only members (spec/testing/changelog/dotfile/community-health, per TR-SPEC-3).

applicability.description: The variance axis - the document analog of code's platform_scope/consumers (baseline §10 M10): which families / topologies the item applies to, and whether it is required. Enables mechanical impact analysis without conditional template assembly.

families.description: Scripting/tool families this item applies to. powershell/bash = script doc-set shape; python = tool doc-set shape (psa.py: no Part A, no TESTING, has VERSION).

topologies.description: Repo topologies this item applies to. subproject = lives under projects/<lang>-<name>/ in the monorepo (inherits monorepo-root community-health/dotfiles). graduated-repo = the spun-out repo root (carries its own community-health).

presence.description: required = the item MUST be present for every applicable target (its family/topology). optional-feature = the item MAY be present (per-consumer opt-in feature, e.g. SPEC A.14 cross-script feature). conditional = present iff a stated condition holds (see 'condition'; e.g. only where the #4 doc-set includes TESTING/CHANGELOG).

condition.description: Required when presence=conditional: the human-readable condition under which the item is present (resolved against the target's #4 doc-set / interface).

source.description: Provenance (non-load-bearing): the M5 register rows (TR-*), Phase-I current-state sections, baseline sections, and/or ADRs this item was derived from. The Tier-P register remains the fuller requirements rationale.

notes.description: Optional free-text clarification for this item.
